newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fresh protest in East Timor after weekend clash.
newsitem.headline: Fresh protest in East Timor after weekend clash.

text.p: East Timorese youths held a fresh 30-minute protest in the territory's capital Dili on Monday after a clash the previous day outside a hotel where a U.N. envoy was staying, police said.

East Timor police chief Colonel Jusuf Muharam told Reuters by telephone that 45 of 48 people detained on Sunday were still in custody. He said about 10 of 11 people injured remained in hospital, but he denied there had been any deaths or serious injuries.
Three of the 48 detained were released when it was found they had not been involved in the protest at the Mahkota Hotel, Muharam said.
He said about 50 people demonstrated at the Becora market in east Dili at about 9:00 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Monday, but they dispersed after 30 minutes and there were no arrests.
Muharam and residents described Dili as calm and normal on Monday.

"Today there was a small demonstration, but it was not violent like yesterday. No one has yet been detained as it was a usual demonstration. If they do not break anything, we do not arrest them," Muharam said.
He added that it was an "anti-integration" protest by people opposed to Indonesian rule in the former Portuguese colony.

Residents said the demonstrators on Sunday had tried to meet Jamsheed Marker, special envoy of U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan for East Timor, after the youths felt frustrated that he was only meeting with government officials and Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo.
Marker, who did not see the demonstration, was flying back to Jakarta on Monday after a three-day visit to East Timor.

Annan last month appointed Marker as his special assistant for East Timor after the U.N. chief pledged to push forward talks between Indonesia and Portugal on the disputed territory's future. The talks have achieved little in 15 years.
Muharam said police seized 12 machettes and knives and 19 banners in Sunday's demonstration.
"There were 11 people injured whom we took to hospital. About 10 remain in hospital," Muharam said.
"Those who were injured broke the glass as they were leaving (the hotel) or were trampled on by others," Muharam said.
"There was only one warning shot and one tear gas canister fired. The warning shot was a rubber bullet to calm the crowd and stop them from becoming violent," he said.

Indonesia invaded East Timor with tacit Western support in December 1975 after the abrupt withdrawal of Portuguese colonial authorities. Indonesia declared the territory its 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
